subject: Deployment enclosure: network map and control-pack for SOC 2 / SIG review
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment enclosure: network map and control-pack for SOC 2 / SIG review

Team —

ACME's security team sent a SIG/CAIQ follow-up focused on "deployment enclosure" controls (they're using our Dedicated + Private diagrams to validate network isolation, KMS boundaries, and egress controls). They've asked for:

- A single-page network enclosure diagram that shows control-plane/data-plane separation for both Dedicated and Private modes (including on-prem connectors).
- Mapping of each network boundary to SIG/CAIQ question IDs (they want explicit callouts).
- Short write-up on how we enforce lateral isolation at the hypervisor/container boundary and any VLAN/overlay translations we do at the edge.

I started an audit packet in Drive (link below) but need the engineering diagram and the control mapping. Can Karthik own the diagram + traffic flow annotations? Kimberly — can you take the SIG/CAIQ mapping (I put a template in Drive). Marcus — please confirm the KMS and key boundary language (we need precise wording for the procurement doc).

Deliverable: single zip we can upload to the ACME portal by Friday EOD (2026-12-04).

Attachments (stubs): redwood_network_enclosure_diagram_v3.pdf (placeholder), control_map_matrix_SIG_CAIX.tsv (workbook), vlan_kms_boundary_summary.docx (KMS blurb draft)

Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/AcmeCo/SIG/2026/enclosure-packet
HubSpot: HS-48721

Thanks — Chloe
Chloe Martin
Manager, Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment enclosure: network map and control-pack for SOC 2 / SIG review

Chloe — will take the diagram. Quick notes / confirmation items while I work:

1) Scope: include both Hosted (for reference), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC + on-prem appliance) topologies. Make the diagram layered: control-plane, management network, data-plane inference pods, and external ingress/egress.

2) Lateral isolation: we'll show the container runtime namespace separation, hardware-enforced MPS/SMC allocations on GPU hosts, and tenant vNIC isolation via SR-IOV or host-side iptables rules (depending on customer flavor). I'll include a small callout box describing continuous KV-cache tenancy segregation (KV cache never persisted to shared storage).

3) VLAN/Overlay note: For Private/VPC we translate customer VLANs at the edge using an isolated NAT/translation layer — we'll call that out as "edge translation gateway"; for Dedicated we keep overlay segments pinned to tenant pools.

4) KMS boundary: Marcus, do you want the key usage diagram as separate file or embedded? If separate, I'll reference it.

I'll attach the first draft (PDF stub) to the Drive packet by EOD today.

—Karthik

From: Matthew Li <matthew.li@acmeco.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acmeco.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment enclosure: network map and control-pack for SOC 2 / SIG review

Chloe / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying asks from ACME Security:

- Can you mark which boundaries are enforced by cloud provider networking primitives (SGs/NACLs, VPC routing) vs. vendor-managed overlay (your edge translation gateway)? We need clear audit evidence.
- Please include a short note on how we can verify the KMS boundary in a Dedicated deployment (e.g., customer-managed keys vs. Redwood-managed keys, and any HSM attestations).
- For Private (on-prem), can you show how the air-gapped deployment prevents any unintended outbound flows (we will run a port-scan during onboarding).

If you can include those in the packet that would be ideal — we aim to close this SIG thread by next Wednesday.

Matt Li
Sr. Security Engineer, AcmeCo
matthew.li@acmeco.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Li <matthew.li@acmeco.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment enclosure: network map and control-pack for SOC 2 / SIG review

Matt — thanks, good feedback. Short update and attachments included in the audit packet:

- Enforcement callouts: the diagram now has color-coded legends that explicitly label which boundary is: (A) cloud-provider enforced (SG/NACL/VPC route), (B) Redwood-managed overlay (edge translation gateway, tenant overlay), or (C) host-level enforcement (iptables, SR-IOV config, GPU isolation).
- KMS boundary: Marcus added a concise two-paragraph summary and a KMS usage flow (see vlan_kms_boundary_summary.docx). For Dedicated we support both customer-managed CMKs in the customer's cloud account (recommended) and Redwood-managed CMKs; the packet includes the steps for an HSM attestation and key import checklist.
- Private / air-gap: the PDF diagram includes an explicit egress block and a validation checklist we run during onboarding (port/egress verification, deterministic DNS allowlist, no default route).

I've attached the three stubs to the Drive packet and uploaded the zipped audit bundle to the HubSpot record. Next actions: Kimberly to finalize SIG/CAIQ mapping (control_map_matrix_SIG_CAIX.tsv) by Monday morning; Karthik will update the diagram per Matt's boundary labels; Marcus will finalize KMS attestation wording. Once those are in, I'll zip and push to ACME portal.

Attachments (stubs in packet): redwood_network_enclosure_diagram_v3.pdf, control_map_matrix_SIG_CAIX.tsv, vlan_kms_boundary_summary.docx

Thanks all — Chloe
